# azurerm

Stores the state as a Blob with the given Key within the Blob Container within [the Blob Storage Account](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-introduction).

This backend supports state locking and consistency checking with Azure Blob Storage native capabilities.

## Authentication

!> **Warning:**  We recommend using environment variables to supply credentials and other sensitive data. If you use `-backend-config` or hardcode these values directly in your configuration, Terraform will include these values in both the `.terraform` subdirectory and in plan files. Refer to [Credentials and Sensitive Data](/terraform/language/backend#credentials-and-sensitive-data) for details.

The `azurerm` backend needs to authenticate to the storage account data plane in order to manipulate the state file blob in the storage account container. In order to do that, it needs to authenticate and to know the data plane URI for the storage account.

The `azurerm` backend supports 5 methods to authenticate to the storage account data plane:

- [Microsoft Entra ID](#microsoft-entra-id) **(Recommended)**
- [SAS Token](#sas-token) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*
- [Access Key](#access-key) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*
- [Access Key Lookup](#access-key-lookup) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*

### Microsoft Entra ID and Access Key Lookup Authentication Types

There are 5 types of Microsoft Entra ID authentication supported, which apply to the Microsoft Entra ID and Access Key Lookup methods.

- OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation **(Recommended)**
  - User Assigned Managed Identity with Federated Credentials **(Recommended)**
  - Service Princial / App Registration with Federated Credentials
- User or System Assigned Managed Identity
  - User Assigned Managed Identity attached to Azure compute instance (agent / runner)
  - System Assigned Managed Identity attached to Azure compute instance (agent / runner)
- Service Principal / App Registration with Client Secret
- Service Principal / App REgistration with Client Certificate
- User Account with Azure CLI only (for local development cycle)

These types can be supplied via inputs or via a pre-authenticated Azure CLI. We cover them in more depth in the following sections.

### Data Plane URI

In most cases, you can infer the data plane URI from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.  Refer to the [storage account overview documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview#standard-endpoints) for more information on the standard endpoints.

If you are using the ['Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview#azure-dns-zone-endpoints-preview), the backend will need to lookup the data plane URI from the management plane. This requires that you set the `lookup_blob_endpoint` configuration option to `true` and the `Reader` role assignment on the storage account.

## Microsoft Entra ID

This method requires a valid Microsoft Entra ID principal and a predictable storage account data plane URI.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `use_azuread_auth` - Set to `true` to use Microsoft Entra ID authentication to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
- `tenant_id` - The tenant ID of the Microsoft Entra ID principal is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Optional Inputs

The following optional argument separates backend environment variables from provider environment variables:

- `environment_variable_suffix` - The suffix appended to supported backend `ARM_*` environment variable names. Defaults to an empty string (unsuffixed behavior). You can also set it with `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX`. Requires Terraform 1.17 with suffix support. This argument applies to all authentication methods.

The following options apply when [looking up the data plane URI](#data-plane-uri) from the management plane. They are not required when the data plane URI can be inferred from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.

- `lookup_blob_endpoint` - Set to `true` to lookup the storage account data plane URI from the management plane. This is required if you are using the 'Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature. Defaults to `false`. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT` environment variable.
- `subscription_id` - The subscription ID of the storage account is required to query the management plane. This is only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
- `resource_group_name` - The resource group name of the storage account is required to query the management plane. This is only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`.

### Select backend environment variables

~> **Version requirement:** Environment variable suffix selection requires a Terraform 1.17 build that includes this feature. Terraform 1.16 does not support it.

Use `environment_variable_suffix` to separate the built-in `azurerm` backend's environment variables from those used by Azure providers. This setting affects the backend only; it does not change provider authentication.

Terraform selects the suffix in this order:

1. The explicit `environment_variable_suffix` backend setting, including an empty string.
1. The `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX` environment variable when the setting is omitted or null.
1. An empty string when neither supplies a value.

An empty suffix preserves the default, unsuffixed environment variables and authentication behavior. Explicitly setting `environment_variable_suffix = ""` overrides even a non-empty or invalid control environment variable. Other string settings retain their normal behavior: non-empty explicit configuration takes precedence over environment defaults.

A non-empty suffix must match `^_[A-Z0-9_]+$`: a leading underscore followed by one or more uppercase ASCII letters, digits, or underscores. For example, `_BACKEND` and `_STATE_2` are valid. Terraform does not trim whitespace and rejects invalid suffixes.

With `environment_variable_suffix = "_BACKEND"`, the backend reads only the selected suffixed `ARM_*` environment variables. For example, it reads `ARM_TENANT_ID_BACKEND`, not `ARM_TENANT_ID`. There is no unsuffixed `ARM_*` fallback. This rule applies to every supported `ARM_*` setting and alias, including credentials, authentication flags, Azure environment settings, and snapshot settings. Alias precedence stays the same. The selector's control variable is always `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX`; Terraform does not append the suffix to it.

Unless stated otherwise, environment variable names on this page describe the default, unsuffixed mode. Append the selected suffix to each supported `ARM_*` name when you enable suffix mode. Empty environment values are ignored. Explicit boolean `false` and the environment value `"false"` are respected.

Suffix mode also changes these authentication defaults:

- Terraform ignores GitHub's native continuous integration (CI) variables `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*`. Explicitly map those values into the selected `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_URL` and `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN` variables so the backend can request tokens.
- Selecting an Azure DevOps service connection through explicit configuration or a suffixed `ARM_*` variable enables the native `SYSTEM_OIDCREQUESTURI` and `SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN` token request defaults. Explicit settings and selected suffixed `ARM_*` request variables take precedence. The backend does not use these native defaults without a selected service connection, and never uses `AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` as a suffix-mode fallback. Native CI variable names are not suffixed.
- Azure CLI authentication defaults to disabled. Enable it explicitly with `use_cli = true` or the selected `ARM_USE_CLI` variable. Missing backend credentials do not fall back to an existing Azure CLI login.
- Managed identity and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) workload identity remain disabled unless you enable their backend settings or selected `ARM_*` flags. Opting into AKS workload identity permits its native `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, and `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` inputs; these names are not suffixed.

In suffix mode, Terraform selects each direct value and file alternative as a pair:

| Direct setting | File setting |
| --- | --- |
| `client_id` | `client_id_file_path` |
| `client_secret` | `client_secret_file_path` |
| `client_certificate` | `client_certificate_path` |
| `oidc_token` | `oidc_token_file_path` |

A non-empty explicit member selects the explicit pair and excludes both environment defaults for that pair. Otherwise, both members come from the selected environment namespace. This prevents a backend file from being paired with a provider's unsuffixed value. Existing client ID, client secret, and OIDC token mismatch checks still apply when you supply both direct and file values.

Choose one OpenID Connect (OIDC) method: an assertion (`oidc_token`, `oidc_token_file_path`, or enabled AKS workload identity), or a token request (`oidc_request_url`, `oidc_request_token`, or `ado_pipeline_service_connection_id`). Explicit assertion settings exclude environment-derived request settings, and explicit request settings exclude environment-derived assertions. Competing explicit methods, or competing methods in the selected environment without an explicit choice, produce a `Conflicting OIDC authentication settings` error.

You can persist the non-secret selector in your backend block or a non-secret `-backend-config` file. Terraform saves explicit backend configuration in `.terraform` and plan files, including an explicitly empty selector. It does not persist an environment-derived selector or environment-derived backend credentials. Supply fresh credentials independently to each plan and apply job. If you use `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX`, supply it for every command, including init, plan, and apply; omitting it restores unsuffixed behavior.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

The recommended data plane role assignment required for this method is:

- `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the storage account container (Recommended for least privilege)

The recommended management plane role assignments required for this method are:

- `Reader` on the storage account *(Only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`)*

### Microsoft Entra ID with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation

OpenID Connect (OIDC) lets your workflow request short-lived credentials instead of storing a client secret. The backend uses those credentials to read and write state. The provider uses its credentials to manage resources. The examples use the `Azure/azapi` provider and the built-in `azurerm` backend; you do not need the AzureRM provider to use this backend.

Choose one complete example for your CI platform and identity configuration. Each includes its own Terraform configuration and workflow or pipeline; you do not need to combine examples.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_oidc` - Set to `true` to use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration or User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

<a id="example-configuration-for-github"></a>

#### GitHub Actions with one backend and provider identity

This example uses one identity for the `azurerm` backend and the `Azure/azapi` provider. Both use OIDC and read the same unsuffixed `ARM_*` environment variables. Leave `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX` unset.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container. Add `Reader` on the storage account only when `lookup_blob_endpoint = true` requires management plane access.
1. Grant the identity permission to manage the example resource group in the subscription.
1. Configure a federated identity credential for the GitHub repository and the branch that runs the workflow, with the `api://AzureADTokenExchange` audience.

##### Configure workflow variables

Create the following GitHub Actions repository variables. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Repository variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` | Tenant ID of the shared identity |
| `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Subscription containing the state account and example resources |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | Client ID of the shared identity |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform version satisfying `required_version` in `main.tf` |

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save the following as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the workflow supplies the storage location during initialization. The empty provider block reads authentication settings from environment variables. The resource block defines a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11.2"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the workflow

Save the following as `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml`. The first Terraform step initializes the backend and installs the provider. The second generates `tfplan`. Both automatically read GitHub's token request URL and token; no manual token mapping is required in unsuffixed mode.

```yaml
name: Plan with one Azure identity

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # Shared backend and provider identity.
      ARM_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      # Non-secret storage location passed during initialization.
      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_CONTAINER_NAME }}
      STATE_KEY: ${{ vars.STATE_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ vars.TERRAFORM_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Initialize backend
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform init -input=false `
            "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

      - name: Plan
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
```

Commit `main.tf` and the workflow file, then run the workflow manually from GitHub Actions. The plan previews changes; it does not create the resource group. A later apply job must supply its own OIDC environment and the same storage configuration. Treat saved plans as sensitive, and do not pass credentials through `-backend-config`.

#### GitHub Actions with separate backend and provider identities

This example uses separate identities for the `azurerm` backend and the `Azure/azapi` provider. Both use OIDC. The backend identity belongs to a different tenant and subscription from the provider identity. The backend reads `ARM_*_BACKEND` variables, while the provider reads unsuffixed `ARM_*` variables.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with suffix support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container. Add `Reader` on the storage account only when `lookup_blob_endpoint = true` requires management plane access.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Configure a federated identity credential on each identity for the same GitHub repository and workflow branch, with the `api://AzureADTokenExchange` audience.

##### Configure workflow variables

Create the following GitHub Actions repository variables. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Repository variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_TENANT_ID` | Provider identity's tenant ID |
| `AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Provider subscription for the example resources |
| `AZAPI_CLIENT_ID` | Provider identity's client ID |
| `STATE_TENANT_ID` | Backend identity's separate tenant ID |
| `STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Backend subscription containing the state account |
| `STATE_CLIENT_ID` | Backend identity's client ID |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version containing suffix support |

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save the following as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the workflow supplies the storage location during initialization. The empty provider block reads authentication settings from environment variables. The resource block defines a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the workflow

Save the following as `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml`. The first Terraform step initializes the backend and installs the provider. The second generates `tfplan`. The job supplies `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX` to both steps. Each step that accesses state maps GitHub's token request inputs into the backend namespace.

```yaml
name: Plan with separate Azure identities

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX: "_BACKEND"

      # Provider identity for the resource tenant and subscription.
      ARM_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"

      # Backend identity for the separate state tenant and subscription.
      ARM_TENANT_ID_BACKEND: ${{ vars.STATE_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID_BACKEND: ${{ vars.STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_CLIENT_ID_BACKEND: ${{ vars.STATE_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_USE_OIDC_BACKEND: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD_BACKEND: "true"

      # Non-secret storage location passed during initialization.
      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_CONTAINER_NAME }}
      STATE_KEY: ${{ vars.STATE_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ vars.TERRAFORM_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Initialize backend
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          # Suffix mode requires explicit GitHub token request inputs.
          $env:ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_URL_BACKEND = $env:ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL
          $env:ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN_BACKEND = $env:ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN

          terraform init -input=false `
            "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

      - name: Plan
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          # Each step has its own environment and token request inputs.
          $env:ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_URL_BACKEND = $env:ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL
          $env:ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN_BACKEND = $env:ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN

          terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
```

Commit `main.tf` and the workflow file, then run the workflow manually from GitHub Actions. The plan previews changes; it does not create the resource group. Both identities use automatic OIDC refresh in their respective tenants. A later apply job must supply the same suffix and storage configuration, its own identity environment variables, and its own token request mappings. Treat saved plans as sensitive, and do not pass credentials through `-backend-config`.

<a id="example-configuration-for-azure-devops"></a>

#### Azure Pipelines with one backend and provider identity

This example uses one Azure Resource Manager service connection with workload identity federation for the `azurerm` backend and the `Azure/azapi` provider. Both use OIDC and read the same unsuffixed `ARM_*` environment variables. Leave `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX` unset.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container. Add `Reader` on the storage account only when `lookup_blob_endpoint = true` requires management plane access.
1. Grant the identity permission to manage the example resource group in the subscription.
1. Configure the service connection with workload identity federation and authorize it for this pipeline. Its federated identity credential must match the service connection.
1. Install the [Terraform extension from Microsoft DevLabs](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-devlabs.custom-terraform-tasks) in your Azure DevOps organization to use `TerraformInstaller@1`.

##### Configure pipeline variables

Create the following Azure Pipelines variables. Use the service connection's name for the task input; the task exposes its ID to Terraform. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Pipeline variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Shared service connection name |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform version satisfying `required_version` in `main.tf` |

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save the following as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the pipeline supplies the storage location during initialization. The empty provider block reads authentication settings from environment variables. The resource block defines a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11.2"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the pipeline

Save the following as `azure-pipelines.yml`. The first Terraform task initializes the backend and installs the provider. The second generates `tfplan`. Each task reads the service connection's identity metadata and receives `System.AccessToken` so Terraform can request and refresh OIDC tokens.

```yaml
trigger: none

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
  - checkout: self

  - task: TerraformInstaller@1
    displayName: "[Terraform] Install Terraform"
    inputs:
      terraformVersion: $(TERRAFORM_VERSION)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Initialize backend"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Shared backend and provider identity from this service connection.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform init -input=false `
          "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"
    env:
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: $(STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME)
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: $(STATE_CONTAINER_NAME)
      STATE_KEY: $(STATE_KEY)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Plan"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Each task supplies its own authentication environment.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
    env:
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"
```

Commit `main.tf` and the pipeline file, create an Azure Pipeline from that YAML file, and run it manually. The plan previews changes; it does not create the resource group. A later apply job must reference the service connection, supply its own `System.AccessToken` and identity environment, and use the same storage configuration. Treat saved plans as sensitive, and do not pass credentials through `-backend-config`.

The backend HCL argument is `ado_pipeline_service_connection_id`. Its environment aliases are `ARM_ADO_PIPELINE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` and `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`, in that order. This example uses the latter. In unsuffixed mode only, `AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` is an additional fallback.

#### Azure Pipelines with separate backend and provider identities

This example uses two Azure Resource Manager service connections with workload identity federation: one for the `azurerm` backend and one for the `Azure/azapi` provider. The connections target different tenants and subscriptions. The backend reads `ARM_*_BACKEND` variables, while the provider reads unsuffixed `ARM_*` variables.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with suffix support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container. Add `Reader` on the storage account only when `lookup_blob_endpoint = true` requires management plane access.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Configure both service connections with workload identity federation and authorize both for this pipeline. Each federated identity credential must match its service connection.
1. Install the [Terraform extension from Microsoft DevLabs](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-devlabs.custom-terraform-tasks) in your Azure DevOps organization to use `TerraformInstaller@1`.

##### Configure pipeline variables

Create the following Azure Pipelines variables. Use each service connection's name for its task input; the tasks expose the IDs to Terraform. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Pipeline variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Provider connection name for the resource tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Backend connection name for the separate state tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version containing suffix support |

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save the following as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the pipeline supplies the storage location during initialization. The empty provider block reads authentication settings from environment variables. The resource block defines a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the pipeline

Save the following as `azure-pipelines.yml`. The first Terraform task initializes the backend and installs the provider using the state service connection. The second generates `tfplan` using the provider connection, while retaining the state identity for backend access. Both tasks run in the same job and working directory. Each task supplies the suffix and its own authentication environment.

```yaml
trigger: none

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
  - checkout: self

  - task: TerraformInstaller@1
    displayName: "[Terraform] Install Terraform"
    inputs:
      terraformVersion: $(TERRAFORM_VERSION)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Initialize backend"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Initialize state with the backend service connection.
        $clientId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $tenantId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $connectionId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID
        $subscriptionId = az account show --query id --output tsv

        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID_BACKEND = $clientId
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID_BACKEND = $tenantId
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID_BACKEND = $subscriptionId
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID_BACKEND = $connectionId

        terraform init -input=false `
          "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

        # Pass only non-secret identity metadata to the next task.
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_CLIENT_ID]$clientId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_TENANT_ID]$tenantId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID]$subscriptionId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID]$connectionId"
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX: "_BACKEND"
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)

      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: $(STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME)
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: $(STATE_CONTAINER_NAME)
      STATE_KEY: $(STATE_KEY)

      ARM_USE_OIDC_BACKEND: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD_BACKEND: "true"

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Plan"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # The provider uses this task's connection; state uses the earlier one.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX: "_BACKEND"
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"

      # Restore the backend identity, not credentials from the previous task.
      ARM_CLIENT_ID_BACKEND: $(STATE_CLIENT_ID)
      ARM_TENANT_ID_BACKEND: $(STATE_TENANT_ID)
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID_BACKEND: $(STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID)
      ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID_BACKEND: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID)
      ARM_USE_OIDC_BACKEND: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD_BACKEND: "true"
```

Commit `main.tf` and the pipeline file, create an Azure Pipeline from that YAML file, and run it manually. The plan previews changes; it does not create the resource group. Both identities use automatic OIDC refresh through their selected service connections. A later apply job must repeat the connection setup, storage configuration, and environment mappings, including the suffix, with its own `System.AccessToken`. Treat saved plans as sensitive, and do not pass credentials through `-backend-config`.

Selecting `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID_BACKEND` enables the backend to read the current job's native token request URL and `SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN`; no manual token request mapping is needed. The connection can come from an earlier task in the same job. `ARM_ADO_PIPELINE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID_BACKEND` remains supported and takes precedence if you set both aliases. The backend does not fall back to unsuffixed connection IDs or the provider task's `AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`.

### Microsoft Entra ID with Compute Attached Managed Identity

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_msi` - Set to `true` to use the managed identity to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.

#### Optional Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are optional for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This is not required for System Assigned Managed Identity. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_msi              = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable. Not required for System Assigned Managed Identity.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Azure CLI

You must have a pre-authenticated Azure CLI session using any supported method.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_cli` - Set to `true` to use the Azure CLI session authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_CLI` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_cli              = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_CLI` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable. Azure CLI will fallback to use the connected tenant ID if not supplied.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Client Secret

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

#### Required Inputs

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
- `client_secret` - The client secret of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_secret        = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Client Certificate

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

#### Required Inputs

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
- `client_certificate_path` - The path to the client certificate bundle is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
- `client_certificate_password` - The password for the client certificate bundle is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_azuread_auth            = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_certificate_path     = "/path/to/bundle.pfx"                   # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
    client_certificate_password = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.
    storage_account_name        = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name              = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                         = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## Access Key

This method requires you find the Access Key for the storage account and supply it to the backend configuration.

The Access Key is then used to directly authenticate to the storage account data plane.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `access_key` - The Access Key of the storage account is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

There are no role assignments required on the storage account for this method as the Access Key is used to authenticate to the data plane.

### Example Configuration

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Consider using OIDC as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    access_key           = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789..."  # Can also be set via `ARM_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                                 # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                                  # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                   # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## SAS Token

This method requires you generate a SAS Token for the storage account container or blob and supply it to the backend configuration.

The SAS Token is then used to directly authenticate to the storage account data plane.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `sas_token` - The SAS Token for the storage account container or blob is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_SAS_TOKEN` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Storage Account Required Permissions

The SAS Token requires `write` and `list` permissions on the container or blob.

### Example Configuration

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Consider using OIDC as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    sas_token            = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789..."  # Can also be set via `ARM_SAS_TOKEN` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                                 # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                                  # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                   # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## Access Key Lookup

This method requires a valid Microsoft Entra ID principal and is a fallback for when Microsoft Entra ID authentication cannot be used on the storage account data plane.

This method queries the management plane to get the storage account Access Key and then uses that Access Key to authenticate to the storage account data plane. It requires elevated permissions on the storage account.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `tenant_id` - The tenant ID of the Microsoft Entra ID principal is required to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
- `subscription_id` - The subscription ID of the storage account is required to query the management plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
- `resource_group_name` - The resource group name of the storage account is required to query the management plane.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Optional Configuration Options

The optional `environment_variable_suffix` argument also applies to this method. It defaults to empty and can be set with `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX`. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for the Terraform 1.17 requirement and selection rules.

These optional configuration options apply when [looking up the data plane URI](#data-plane-uri) from the management plane. They are not required when the data plane URI can be inferred from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.

- `lookup_blob_endpoint` - Set to `true` to lookup the storage account data plane URI from the management plane. This is required if you are using the 'Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature. Defaults to `false`. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

The recommended data plane role assignment required for this method is:

- `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the storage account container (Recommended for least privilege)

The recommended management plane role assignments required for this method are:

- `Reader` on the storage account
- `Storage Account Key Operator Service Role` on the storage account

### Access Key Lookup with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation

OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation is the recommended method for this scenario.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_oidc` - Set to `true` to use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration or User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

<a id="example-configuration-for-github-1"></a>

#### GitHub Actions with access key lookup

In default, unsuffixed mode, GitHub's ID token environment variables are automatically found. With suffix mode, explicitly map the token request variables as shown in [GitHub Actions with separate backend and provider identities](#github-actions-with-separate-backend-and-provider-identities).

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_oidc             = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

<a id="example-configuration-for-azure-devops-1"></a>

#### Azure Pipelines with access key lookup

In default, unsuffixed mode, Azure DevOps token endpoint variables are automatically found. Supply `ado_pipeline_service_connection_id` or one of its environment aliases. Refer to [Azure Pipelines with one backend and provider identity](#azure-pipelines-with-one-backend-and-provider-identity) for the service connection setup.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_oidc                         = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    ado_pipeline_service_connection_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` environment variable.
    tenant_id                        = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id                  = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                        = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    resource_group_name              = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name             = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name                   = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                              = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Access Key Lookup with Client Secret

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_secret        = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Access Key Lookup with Client Certificate

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    tenant_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id             = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_certificate_path     = "/path/to/bundle.pfx"                   # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
    client_certificate_password = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name        = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name              = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                         = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## terraform_remote_state Data Source

To use the `terraform_remote_state` data source with the `azurerm` backend, you must use the exact same configuration as you would for the `backend` block in your configuration.

For example to use [Direct Microsoft Entra ID authentication with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation for GitHub](#microsoft-entra-id-with-openid-connect--workload-identity-federation) you would use the following configuration:

```hcl
data "terraform_remote_state" "foo" {
  backend = "azurerm"
  config = {
    use_oidc             = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # There is not environment variable support for this input.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # There is not environment variable support for this input.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # There is not environment variable support for this input.
  }
}
```

## Configuration Variables

!> **Warning:**  We recommend using environment variables to supply credentials and other sensitive data. If you use `-backend-config` or hardcode these values directly in your configuration, Terraform will include these values in both the `.terraform` subdirectory and in plan files. Refer to [Credentials and Sensitive Data](/terraform/language/backend#credentials-and-sensitive-data) for details.

For more information on when each of these configuration settings is required, refer to the previous sections of this page.

The following configuration options are supported:

* `environment_variable_suffix` - (Optional) Selects the suffix appended to supported `ARM_*` environment variables. Can also be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_SUFFIX` when omitted or null. Defaults to empty (unsuffixed behavior). An explicit empty string overrides the control environment variable. A non-empty value, such as `_BACKEND`, enables strict suffix mode with no unsuffixed fallback. Requires Terraform 1.17 with suffix support. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for validation, precedence, and authentication rules.

* `storage_account_name` - (Required) The Name of [the Storage Account](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/storage_account).

* `container_name` - (Required) The Name of [the Storage Container](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/storage_container) within the Storage Account.

* `key` - (Required) The name of the Blob used to retrieve/store Terraform's State file inside the Storage Container.

* `environment` - (Optional) The Azure Environment which should be used. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_ENVIRONMENT` environment variable. Possible values are `public`, `china`  and `usgovernment`. Defaults to `public`.

* `metadata_host` - (Optional) The Hostname of the Azure Metadata Service (for example `management.azure.com`), used to obtain the Cloud Environment when using a Custom Azure Environment. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_METADATA_HOSTNAME` Environment Variable.

* `lookup_blob_endpoint` - (Optional) Set to `true` to look up the Storage Account Data Plane URI from the Management Plane. Defaults to `false`. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

* `snapshot` - (Optional) Set to `true` to snapshot the Blob used to store the Terraform state file before use. Defaults to `false`. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_SNAPSHOT` environment variable.

* `tenant_id` - (Optional) The Tenant ID of the principal. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.

* `use_azuread_auth` - (Optional) Whether Microsoft Entra ID Authentication for storage account data plane authentication. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.

* `subscription_id` - (Optional) The Subscription ID of the storage account required for management plane authentication. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.

* `resource_group_name` - (Optional) The Name of the Resource Group in which the Storage Account exists required for management plane authentication.

* `access_key` - (Optional) The Access Key used to authenticate to the storage account data plane with the [Direct Access Key](#direct-access-key) authenticaton method. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.

* `sas_token` - (Optional) The SAS Token used to authenticate to the storage account data plane with the [Direct SAS Token](#direct-sas-token) authentication method. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_SAS_TOKEN` environment variable.

* `use_cli` - (Optional) Set to `true` to use the Azure CLI session for authentication to the storage account management and data plane. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_CLI` environment variable. Defaults to `true` in unsuffixed mode and `false` in suffix mode. In suffix mode, enable it explicitly in configuration or through the selected suffixed variable.

* `use_oidc` - (Optional) Set to `true` to use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation authentication for authentication to the storage account management and data plane. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.

* `client_id` - (Optional) The Client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Principal required for some authentication sub-types. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

* `ado_pipeline_service_connection_id` - (Optional) The Azure DevOps service connection ID for OIDC authentication. In unsuffixed mode, the backend uses the first non-empty value from `ARM_ADO_PIPELINE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`, `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`, or `AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`. Suffix mode uses only the two suffixed `ARM_*` aliases, in the same order.

* `oidc_request_url` - (Optional) The URL of the OIDC broker from which to request an ID token. In unsuffixed mode, the backend uses the first non-empty value from `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_URL`, `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL`, or `SYSTEM_OIDCREQUESTURI`. Suffix mode uses the selected `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_URL` variable, followed by `SYSTEM_OIDCREQUESTURI` only when you select a backend service connection. GitHub requires explicit mapping into the suffixed variable.

* `oidc_request_token` - (Optional) The bearer token for the request to the OIDC broker. In unsuffixed mode, the backend uses the first non-empty value from `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN`, `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`, or `SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN`. Suffix mode uses the selected `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN` variable, followed by `SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN` only when you select a backend service connection. GitHub requires explicit mapping into the suffixed variable.

* `oidc_token` - (Optional) The ID Token when authenticating using OpenID Connect. This is only required for advanced scenarios or third party integrations. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_OIDC_TOKEN` environment variable.

* `oidc_token_file_path` - (Optional) The path to a file containing an ID token when authenticating using OpenID Connect. This is only required for advanced scenarios or third party integrations. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE_PATH` environment variable.

* `use_aks_workload_identity` (Optional) Set to `true` to use Azure AKS Workload Identity for authentication. This is only required for advanced scenarios or third party integrations. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_AKS_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` environment variable.

* `use_msi` - (Optional) Set to `true` to use a Compute Attached Managed Service Identity for authentication to the storage account management and data planes. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.

* `msi_endpoint` - (Optional) The path to a custom Managed Service Identity endpoint which is automatically determined if not specified. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_MSI_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

* `client_id_file_path` (Optional) The path to a file containing the Client ID which should be used. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_CLIENT_ID_FILE_PATH` Environment Variable.

* `client_certificate_password` - (Optional) The password associated with the Client Certificate specified in `client_certificate_path`. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.

* `client_certificate_path` - (Optional) The path to the PFX file used as the Client Certificate when authenticating as a Service Principal. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.

* `client_certificate` - (Optional) Base64 encoded PKCS#12 certificate bundle to use when authenticating as a Service Principal using a Client Certificate. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE` environment variable.

* `client_id_file_path` (Optional) The path to a file containing the Client ID which should be used. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_CLIENT_ID_FILE_PATH` Environment Variable.

* `client_secret` - (Optional) The Client Secret of the Service Principal. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.

* `client_secret_file_path` - (Optional) The path to a file containing the Client Secret which should be used. This can also be sourced from the `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE_PATH` Environment Variable.
